text:
Marathon Petroleum rallied 3.4% today, reversing some of the steep losses from earlier in the week. The bounce comes as oil prices stabilized and then firmed — U.S. crude rose to $99.64 a barrel today after dipping below $90 last week on hopes of an Iran ceasefire. Refineries are running at 94.5% capacity, and with gasoline and diesel inventories at healthy levels, the market appears to be pricing in steadier energy demand and tighter crude supplies if geopolitical tensions ease or persist.

The stock's sharp two-week decline reflects real uncertainty: earlier this week, falling oil prices on talk of peace with Iran spooked refinery stocks, since lower crude means tighter margins for refiners. Today's rebound suggests the market is cautiously repricing that risk as diplomacy stalls and oil finds a floor — but the back-and-forth swings show investors are still sorting through whether Middle East tensions will cool or simmer on.
